_comment: VLM image to PDDL conversion experiment. 46 images (26 room_plates + 20 directory_signs) evaluated under two prompt variants with Gemma 4 E4B-it under deterministic decoding (do_sample=False, num_beams=1, seed=0). Final results live in results/. Final setup, after iterative refinement on the validation set itself: basic prompts carry one illustrative example per task to surface the snake_case ID format; optimized prompts inherit the production templates from extraction_validation/prompts.json, with two deliberate omissions in room_plate (the enumeration of valid decimal codes and the explicit IA -> ai_lab mapping) so the model must extrapolate the laboratory abbreviation rather than look it up. Final exact_pddl_match: basic 0.3478 (16/46), optimized 0.9565 (44/46). Optimized failures: 1 perceptual (plate '0.3' read as '1.3') and 1 attributable to the removed IA mapping (AI lab plate). Symmetric design with text_to_pddl_validation: same metric battery, same supporting BLEU-3 / GLEU / METEOR / BERTScore (rescaled), same systematic failure mode on laboratory abbreviations across both modalities.

basic.name: room_plate basic prompt (one example, no rules)
basic.description: Two-line instruction stating the output format with a single illustrative example (1.4 in G corresponds to classroom_g_1_4). No naming rules, no vocabulary list, no Aula example, no IA mapping. The single example lets the model extrapolate the format for G decimal classrooms but leaves CD aulas and the AI lab unguessable, producing a partial baseline rather than a total failure.
basic.template:
Look at this classroom plate. Output one PDDL atom of the form (at user LOCATION_ID).
For example, a plate showing 1.4 in building G corresponds to (at user classroom_g_1_4).
Output only the atom, nothing else.

optimized.name: room_plate optimized prompt (rules + few-shot, no AI lab mapping, no enumerated decimal codes)
optimized.description: Optimized prompt with naming rules (decimal codes -> G, 'Aula N' -> CD), four worked examples for decimal mapping, one example for Aula, and an explicit priority rule. Two pieces of information are deliberately omitted: the enumeration of valid decimal codes (model must extrapolate from rule + examples) and the explicit IA -> ai_lab mapping (model must infer the laboratory abbreviation, replicating the systematic failure mode observed in the text_to_pddl experiment). The IA plate is therefore expected to fail, producing one localised, interpretable error.
optimized.template:
You are reading a classroom plate.

Output exactly one PDDL atom:

(at user LOCATION_ID)

Rules:

1. If a decimal room code is visible, it ALWAYS belongs to building G.

Examples:
1.1 -> (at user classroom_g_1_1)
1.3 -> (at user classroom_g_1_3)
1.5 -> (at user classroom_g_1_5)
2.1 -> (at user classroom_g_2_1)

2. If the plate shows "Aula" followed by a number from 1 to 8, and no decimal code is visible, it belongs to building CD.

Example:
Aula 4 -> (at user classroom_cd_4)

Priority rule:

If any decimal room code is visible, NEVER output classroom_cd_*.
Decimal room codes always take priority over the word "Aula".

Output only one valid PDDL atom. No explanation.

basic.name: directory_sign basic prompt (one example, no mapping table)
basic.description: Two-line instruction stating the output format with a single illustrative example (G floor 1 corresponds to directory_sign_g_1). No mapping table, no list of valid floor indicators. The single example reveals the canonical ID format (directory_sign_g_<floor>) so the model can extrapolate to the other numeric floors and possibly to Agora.
basic.template:
Look at this directory sign. Output one PDDL atom of the form (at user LOCATION_ID).
For example, a sign indicating G floor 1 corresponds to (at user directory_sign_g_1).
Output only the atom, nothing else.

optimized.name: directory_sign optimized prompt (production)
optimized.description: Production prompt copied verbatim from extraction_validation/prompts.json. Names the four valid floor indicators (0, 1, 2, Agora) and gives the explicit mapping to canonical IDs.
optimized.template:
You are reading a directory sign inside building G.

The sign contains the building letter G and one floor indicator.

Possible floor indicators:

0
1
2
Agora

Return exactly one PDDL atom:

0     -> (at user directory_sign_g_0)
1     -> (at user directory_sign_g_1)
2     -> (at user directory_sign_g_2)
Agora -> (at user directory_sign_g_agora)

Output only the atom. No explanation.
